title: Cloud Run 5xx After Deployment
content: When 5xx errors start immediately after a Cloud Run deployment, compare the new revision with the previous healthy revision. Check container startup failures, application exceptions, missing environment variables or secrets, IAM changes, dependency connectivity, and health/startup behavior. Review Cloud Logging for the failing revision. If impact is high, shift traffic back to the last known-good revision while investigating.

title: Cloud Run High Latency
content: For Cloud Run latency, separate platform startup time from application processing time and downstream dependency time. Check request latency percentiles, instance count, concurrency, CPU allocation, cold starts, database/API latency, and model inference latency. Distributed traces should identify which span dominates the end-to-end request. Consider minimum instances for cold-start-sensitive workloads and tune concurrency based on CPU and memory behavior.

title: GKE CrashLoopBackOff Troubleshooting
content: For CrashLoopBackOff, inspect pod status and recent events, then inspect current and previous container logs. Validate the container command, environment variables, mounted secrets/config maps, resource limits, probes, and application startup dependencies. Check for OOMKilled, permission errors, missing configuration, or failed network dependencies before restarting repeatedly.

title: Application Memory Spike
content: When memory rises unexpectedly, correlate memory usage with request volume, payload size, concurrency, cache growth, and recent deployments. Inspect for OOM events and garbage collection pressure. Use traces to identify unusually large or long-lived operations. In containers, confirm memory limits and avoid treating a higher limit as the root-cause fix if the application is leaking memory.

title: Downstream API Timeout
content: For downstream API timeouts, use distributed tracing to identify the slow dependency and quantify its contribution to total latency. Check timeout configuration, DNS/network connectivity, dependency health, rate limits, and error codes. Use bounded retries with backoff only for retryable failures. Consider circuit breaking or graceful degradation when a noncritical dependency is unavailable.

title: RAG Quality Degradation
content: When RAG quality degrades, separate retrieval quality from generation quality. Record the user question, retrieved document identifiers and relevance scores, and final answer while avoiding sensitive content. Evaluate groundedness/faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision or retrieval quality, and hallucination risk. Use a golden dataset for regression tests and sampled production evaluations for live quality trends.

title: LLM Invocation Latency or Timeout
content: For LLM latency, trace model invocation separately from retrieval and tool execution. Track model name, request duration, errors, and token-related workload indicators when available. Reduce unnecessary context, enforce timeouts, and distinguish provider latency from application-side queueing or preprocessing. Use fallback behavior for user-facing flows when appropriate.

title: OpenTelemetry Distributed Tracing
content: Instrument the incoming request as a parent span and create child spans around agent execution, retrieval, tool calls, model invocations, and evaluation. Propagate trace context across service boundaries. Add low-cardinality attributes that help debugging and avoid sensitive prompts or customer data. Export OTLP telemetry to the observability backend and use trace IDs to correlate a user request with backend execution.
